question: Can a double-tapped breaker be fixed with a pigtail, and when isn't that the right fix?
verdictConfirmed: Usually. A pigtail moves the joint into a listed splice (IRC E3406.11) so one wire lands on a terminal not identified for two (E3406.10). It doesn't fix mismatched wire sizes (E3705.5.3), circuits that must stand alone (E3703.2-E3703.4), neutrals (E3706.4) or aluminum without identified connectors. Square D QO 10-30 A breakers are rated for two copper wires, but not their AFI/CAFI/GFI/DF versions.

facts.claim: IRC 2021 E3406.10 (NEC 110.14(A)): connections to terminals by pressure connectors, splices to flexible leads, or binding screws for 10 AWG and smaller; terminals for more than one conductor and for aluminum conductors shall be identified for the application.
facts.quote: Connection of conductors to terminal parts shall be made without damaging the conductors and shall be made by means of pressure connectors, including set-screw type, by means of splices to flexible leads, or for conductor sizes of 10 AWG and smaller, by means of wire binding screws or studs and nuts having upturned lugs or the equivalent. Terminals for more than one conductor and terminals for connecting aluminum conductors shall be identified for the application. [110.14(A)]

facts.claim: IRC 2021 E3406.11 (NEC 110.14(B)): conductors spliced or joined with splicing devices listed for the purpose; splices covered with equivalent insulation or a listed insulating device.
facts.quote: Conductors shall be spliced or joined with splicing devices listed for the purpose. Splices and joints and the free ends of conductors shall be covered with an insulation equivalent to that of the conductors or with an insulating device listed for the purpose. [110.14(B)]

facts.claim: IRC 2021 E3706.4 (NEC 408.41): each grounded conductor terminates in the panelboard on an individual terminal not also used for another conductor (exception: parallel conductors on a terminal identified for more than one).
facts.quote: Each grounded conductor shall terminate within the panelboard on an individual terminal that is not also used for another conductor, except that grounded conductors of circuits with parallel conductors shall be permitted to terminate on a single terminal where the terminal is identified for connection of more than one conductor. (408.41 and 408.41 Exception)

facts.claim: IRC 2021 E3907.1 and E3907.1.1 (NEC 312.8): the wiring space in a switch or overcurrent device enclosure may hold splices and taps if conductors fill no more than 40 percent of any cross section and conductors, splices and taps no more than 75 percent.
facts.quote: The wiring space within enclosures for switches and overcurrent devices shall be permitted for other wiring and equipment in accordance with Sections E3907.1.1 and E3907.1.2. [312.8] ... Where the wiring space of enclosures for switches or overcurrent device contains conductors feeding through, spliced, or tapping off to other enclosures, switches, or overcurrent devices, the following conditions shall be met: 1. The total area of all conductors installed at any cross section of the wiring space shall not exceed 40 percent of the cross-sectional area of that space. 2. The total area of all conductors, splices and taps installed at any cross section of the wiring space shall not exceed 75 percent of the cross-sectional area of that space.

facts.claim: IRC 2021 E3705.5.3 and Table E3705.5.3 (NEC 240.4(D)): maximum breaker for copper 14 AWG is 15 amps, 12 AWG 20 amps, 10 AWG 30 amps.
facts.quote: Except as specifically permitted by Section E3705.5.4, the rating of overcurrent protection devices shall not exceed the ratings shown in Table E3705.5.3 for the conductors specified therein. [240.4(D)] ... COPPER Size (AWG) Maximum overcurrent-protection-device rating (amps) 14 15; 12 20; 10 30

facts.claim: Schneider Electric FAQ FA97891 (last modified 10/28/2025): 10 to 30 A QO breakers are rated for 2 conductors under 1 terminal for copper #14-#10; 1 conductor #14-#8 Cu or Al; applies to QO and QOB, 1, 2 and 3 pole; not QOT; not suffix GFI, AFI, CAFI, DF, EPD or EPE.
facts.quote: Yes, 10 to 30 A QO breakers are rated to accept 2 conductors under 1 terminal for copper wire size #14-#10.
